tone_statements.translation: TONES: ma53 ma55 ma35 ma31. In [JZ-Nusu] (Sun & Liu 1986) tones are represented by Chao tone letters, not numbers. Most tense rhymes carry tone /53/, which is then realized as [54]. /55/ is phonetically [44]; /35/ is [24]. /31/ is realized as [21] in monosyllables, [11] in prefix syllables, and [22] medially in polysyllabic words.

Inventory compiled from Sun & Liu 1986 (pp. 3-16) and ZMYYC 1991 (#45, pp. 297-302): initials, rhymes and four tones (53, 55, 35, 31) with allotone notes ('/31/ is realized as [21] in monosyllables, [11] in prefix syllables, and [22] medially in polysyllabic words'); no STRESS/ACCENT heading and no mention of stress for Nusu (the monograph does have such headings for other languages, e.g. Qiang Mawo, Newari).

tone.says: Four tones for Central (Bijiang) Nusu: /53/, /55/, /35/, /31/ (STEDT font digits), with allotony: most tense (constricted) rhymes take /53/ realized [54]; /55/ is phonetically [44]; /35/ is [24]; /31/ is [21] in monosyllables, [11] in prefix syllables, [22] word-medially. Tense vs lax (constricted) rhymes listed separately, i.e. phonation is treated as a rhyme feature, tone as pitch.
